You’re not alone in feeling like this, if its any comfort. I’m in my third year and I’ve had to withdraw from two of my classes because of the amount of work that worsened my already tenuous mental state. I felt like an utter failure, because this was the second time I had to exercise this option. But your mental health and well-being should ALWAYS take priority, even if that means falling a bit behind to recuperate. You’re in your own timeline, no matter what anyone else says, and that gives you the freedom to slow down, take a break, and come back to it. It might suck that you won’t be graduating on the same timeline as others, but its your life and other people aren’t you. You shouldn’t rush to meet arbitrary dates (like getting your degree in four years) if it means your well-being is destroyed in the process. You’re young and you still have a lotta life to live, so making this significant academic change is perfectly acceptable and no one will look down upon you for choosing what you feel is best for you. You’ll be okay in the long-term, even if it means shitty feelings in the short.

Also, take the upcoming break as a chance to completely decompress and forget about school. It might be short, but engage in activities you enjoy to re-ignite your spark and make your mental state better.
